title: Wait for async test conditions by bounded polling, not fixed sleeps
answers: How should a test wait for a server or background job to be ready?
Why is time.sleep flaky in MLflow tests?
Test fails intermittently because the server has not started yet, what to do?
Should I use time.sleep before asserting on an async result in a test?
body:
Convention: when a test waits for an asynchronous condition (server startup, background work), poll with a monotonic deadline instead of calling time.sleep(N) once.
Pattern: deadline = time.monotonic() + 30; loop while time.monotonic() < deadline, check the condition, sleep a short interval (about 0.5s); use a while/else that raises TimeoutError with a clear message.
Why: a fixed sleep slows fast runs and is too short on slow CI machines, and when it fails it does not say the system was still starting.
Exception: a fixed sleep is fine when elapsed time itself is the behavior under test.
The section lives in the testing guidance of the python-style skill; keep new test waits consistent with it.
applies: Applies to writing or reviewing Python tests in this repository that wait on anything asynchronous; does not cover production code retry logic.
says: Automated test suite intermittently fails during server startup on continuous integration runners.
Tests verifying background tasks fail randomly because the server has not finished starting.
Test execution is unnecessarily slow due to hardcoded wait timers between actions.
Poll for server readiness and background task completion rather than using fixed pauses.
